governance_justification: China has no comprehensive AI statute, but binding, technology-specific departmental rules led by the CAC (recommendation algorithms, deep synthesis, generative AI, labelling, anthropomorphic AI) sit on horizontal NPC Standing Committee statutes (PIPL, Cybersecurity Law), so it is neither a single-statute nor a purely sectoral model.
institutional_map: The Cyberspace Administration of China (CAC) is the hub: it issued or co-issued all five coded departmental rules, coordinates their supervision, and runs the algorithm filing regime into which deep synthesis, generative AI and anthropomorphic services are channelled, with provincial cyberspace offices receiving filings and anthropomorphic-service security assessments. The PIPL and the Cybersecurity Law are NPC Standing Committee statutes, not CAC instruments; under them the CAC coordinates while State Council departments enforce within their remits. Co-regulators named in the rules act in their own fields: MIIT and telecommunications authorities, the Ministry of Public Security, SAMR (pricing and consumer issues), NRTA and press-and-publication authorities (audiovisual and published content), and NDRC, MoE and MoST under the generative AI Measures. Overlaps arise between the CAC and SAMR on algorithmic price discrimination and between the CAC and NRTA on synthetic audiovisual content.
conv: Filing and security assessment at or shortly after launch make registration a core control point for public-facing AI services, echoing the EU AI Act's registration of high-risk systems, though China triggers it by a service's public-opinion or mobilisation capacity (and, for anthropomorphic services, launch and user scale) rather than by risk tier.

Duties to label AI-generated content and to tell users they are dealing with AI parallel the transparency duties spreading across the atlas, such as Article 50 of the EU AI Act, and PIPL Art. 24 echoes GDPR Art. 22-style safeguards against solely automated decisions.
gaps: There is no horizontal AI law or general legal definition of AI, and duties attach by technology or service type to a 'service provider' (the deep synthesis rules' 'technical supporter' is the main exception), so a system outside the defined categories is reached only through general data and cybersecurity law.

Individual redress is thin: there is no express right to human review, explanation rights hinge on an undefined 'major impact', and the rules borrow sanctions from other laws, with their own modest fines (at most RMB 100,000-200,000) only as a fallback; the coded rules also target public-facing services, leaving in-house R&D to separate ethics-review rules and state use of AI largely to the PIPL.
assume: Excluded as outside the team's coding: the MIIT-led AI ethics review Measures (trial, 2026), the AI Safety Governance Framework 2.0, the Data Security Law and GB/T 45654-2025; mandatory standard GB 45438-2025 is folded into the Labelling row. No AI Law had been enacted or, as far as the editors could find, submitted to the NPC Standing Committee, and no rule taking effect between October and 19 November 2026 supersedes a coded row. Translation risk: there are no official English texts; English titles and terms such as 备案 (filing) and 重大影响 (major impact) are the editors' renderings, with Chinese titles in original_title. Judgement calls (single team): Labelling Measures kept as binding subordinate rules though issued by notice, because they name enforcing departments and incorporate a mandatory standard. Risk is coded Present only where the instrument itself sorts services into levels with different duties (algorithm, deep synthesis and generative AI rules: public-opinion or mobilisation services must file and be security-assessed); the anthropomorphic rules are Absent because every service is assessed at launch and filed. Status verified as of 19-11-2026.

instruments.name: Cybersecurity Law of the People's Republic of China (Art. 20, inserted 2025)
instruments.original_title: 中华人民共和国网络安全法（第二十条）
instruments.systems: AI generally, through a new state-policy article on AI research, infrastructure, ethics and safety supervision; AI is not defined
instruments.trigger: None for firms: the article directs state action; the amendment, including Art. 20, has applied since 1 January 2026
instruments.duty_note: Commits the state to support AI research, training-data and computing infrastructure, improve AI ethics norms and strengthen risk monitoring, assessment and safety supervision
instruments.enf: The national cyberspace department coordinates, with telecommunications, public security and other State Council departments, under the Law generally
instruments.remedy: No sanction attaches to Art. 20; the amendment raised the Law's general fines to as much as RMB 10 million for the most serious breaches (Arts. 61, 69)
instruments.gap: The AI article is promotional: it places no enforceable duty or liability on developers or deployers, so it signals policy direction without adding operative AI obligations.
instruments.citation: Decision of the NPC Standing Committee on Amending the Cybersecurity Law of the People's Republic of China (adopted 28 October 2025, President's Order No. 61, in force 1 January 2026), new Art. 20

instruments.name: Personal Information Protection Law of the People's Republic of China
instruments.original_title: 中华人民共和国个人信息保护法
instruments.systems: Automated decision-making using personal information, defined in Art. 73(2); AI itself is not defined
instruments.trigger: Processing personal information, including for automated decision-making or personalised push and marketing
instruments.duties: Transparency; Impact assessment; Audit; Data governance
instruments.duty_note: Keep automated decisions transparent and fair with no unreasonable price discrimination, offer a non-personalised option or easy opt-out for push and marketing, and assess impact before using automated decision-making (Arts. 24, 55)
instruments.enf: The CAC coordinates; State Council departments and local governments enforce within their remits (Art. 60)
instruments.remedy: Rectification, warning, confiscation and app suspension, with fines up to RMB 1 million on refusal to rectify; in serious cases up to RMB 50 million or 5% of prior-year turnover (Art. 66); presumed-fault damages (Art. 69)
instruments.gap: The Art. 24 explanation and refusal rights apply only to decisions with an undefined 'major impact', the refusal right only to decisions made solely by automated means, and there is no express right to human review, so most partly automated decisions escape them.
instruments.citation: Personal Information Protection Law of the People's Republic of China (adopted by the NPC Standing Committee 20 August 2021, President's Order No. 91, in force 1 November 2021), Arts. 24, 55, 73(2)

instruments.name: Provisions on the Administration of Algorithmic Recommendation in Internet Information Services
instruments.original_title: 互联网信息服务算法推荐管理规定
instruments.systems: Services using generation/synthesis, personalised push, ranking, search/filtering or scheduling/decision algorithms to supply information (Art. 2); AI is not defined
instruments.trigger: Using algorithmic recommendation technology to provide internet information services in mainland China; in force 1 March 2022
instruments.duties: Transparency; Labelling; Risk management; Human oversight; Data governance; Registration or filing; Prohibition
instruments.duty_note: Disclose and explain the basic logic of recommendation, review algorithms regularly, label unlabelled synthetic content, and file and security-assess services with public-opinion or mobilisation capacity
instruments.tiers: Two levels: services with public-opinion attributes or social-mobilisation capacity must file within 10 working days of launch and undergo security assessment (Arts. 24, 27); other services do not; Art. 23 also mandates a graded, categorised management system without naming tiers
instruments.enf: The CAC coordinates; telecommunications, public security and market regulation departments supervise within their remits (Art. 3)
instruments.remedy: Sanctions under other laws and administrative regulations first; only where none applies, warning, criticism and rectification, then suspension of updates and a fine of RMB 10,000-100,000 for refusal or serious cases (Art. 31); some breaches go wholly to other rules (Art. 32); revocation of filing (Art. 33)
instruments.gap: Users can switch off personalisation, delete tags and complain, but an explanation is owed only where an algorithm has an undefined 'major impact' on their rights and there is no right to human review of an outcome; the rules' own fine (up to RMB 100,000) is only a fallback where other laws are silent.
instruments.citation: Order No. 9 of the CAC, MIIT, MPS and SAMR, Provisions on the Administration of Algorithmic Recommendation in Internet Information Services (adopted 16 November 2021, promulgated 31 December 2021, in force 1 March 2022)

instruments.name: Provisions on the Administration of Deep Synthesis in Internet Information Services
instruments.original_title: 互联网信息服务深度合成管理规定
instruments.systems: Deep synthesis technology, i.e. deep learning, virtual reality and other generative or synthetic algorithms producing text, audio, images, video and virtual scenes (Art. 23); AI is not defined
instruments.trigger: Providing deep synthesis services, or technical support for them, in mainland China; in force 10 January 2023
instruments.duties: Labelling; Risk management; Data governance; Registration or filing; Prohibition
instruments.duty_note: Verify user identity, review inputs and outputs, label synthetic content, secure training data, security-assess biometric-editing tools and file services with public-opinion or mobilisation capacity
instruments.tiers: Services likely to confuse or mislead the public need prominent labels (Art. 17(1)); other services must offer a labelling function (Art. 17(2)); filing and security assessment for services with public-opinion or mobilisation capacity
instruments.enf: The CAC coordinates; telecommunications and public security departments supervise within their remits (Arts. 3, 21)
instruments.remedy: Penalties under other laws and administrative regulations, heavier for serious consequences; orders to suspend services; public-security penalties or criminal liability (Arts. 21-22)
instruments.gap: Sanctions are wholly borrowed from other laws, so there is no deepfake-specific penalty, and a person depicted in synthetic content gets no direct remedy beyond the consent prompt for biometric editing (Art. 14).
instruments.citation: Order No. 12 of the CAC, MIIT and MPS, Provisions on the Administration of Deep Synthesis in Internet Information Services (adopted 3 November 2022, signed 25 November 2022, published 11 December 2022, in force 10 January 2023)

instruments.name: Interim Measures for the Administration of Generative Artificial Intelligence Services
instruments.original_title: 生成式人工智能服务管理暂行办法
instruments.systems: Generative AI technology, defined as models and related technology able to generate text, images, audio and video (Art. 22), used to serve the public in mainland China; R&D not offered to the public is excluded (Art. 2)
instruments.trigger: Providing generative AI services, including via API, to the public in mainland China; in force 15 August 2023
instruments.duties: Transparency; Labelling; Risk management; Data governance; Registration or filing; Prohibition
instruments.duty_note: Use lawful training data and labelling rules, prevent discrimination and prohibited content, label generated content, and security-assess and file services with public-opinion or mobilisation capacity
instruments.tiers: Two levels: services with public-opinion attributes or social-mobilisation capacity need security assessment and algorithm filing (Art. 17); other services do not; Arts. 3 and 16 envisage further classified, graded rules not yet set in the text
instruments.enf: Cyberspace, development and reform, education, science and technology, industry and IT, public security, broadcasting and press-and-publication departments within their remits (Art. 16)
instruments.remedy: Penalties under the Cybersecurity, Data Security, Personal Information Protection and Science and Technology Progress Laws; otherwise warning, criticism, rectification and suspension of services (Art. 21)
instruments.gap: It excludes R&D not offered to the public and leaves its promised graded rules to future instruments, so pre-release frontier-model development is largely outside its reach, and it carries no AI-specific fine.
instruments.citation: Order No. 15 of the CAC, NDRC, MoE, MoST, MIIT, MPS and NRTA, Interim Measures for the Administration of Generative Artificial Intelligence Services (adopted 23 May 2023, signed 10 July 2023, in force 15 August 2023)

instruments.name: Measures for Labelling AI-Generated Synthetic Content
instruments.original_title: 人工智能生成合成内容标识办法（国信办通字〔2025〕2号）
instruments.systems: AI-generated or synthetic text, images, audio, video and virtual scenes from services within the algorithm, deep synthesis and generative AI rules (Arts. 2-3); AI is not defined
instruments.trigger: Providing generation or synthesis services, distributing content online, or listing apps that offer such services; in force 1 September 2025
instruments.duty_note: Add explicit labels and metadata (implicit) labels to AI content, have distribution platforms detect and flag it, and bar malicious removal or forgery of labels; technical rules are in mandatory standard GB 45438-2025
instruments.enf: Cyberspace, telecommunications, public security and radio and television departments within their remits (Art. 13)
instruments.remedy: No sanction of its own; breaches are handled under other laws, administrative regulations and departmental rules (Art. 13)
instruments.gap: Implicit metadata labels are easily stripped as content moves between platforms, so traceability rests on platform detection and user self-declaration; issued by notice rather than as a numbered Order, it has no sanction clause of its own.
instruments.citation: CAC, MIIT, MPS and NRTA, Measures for Labelling AI-Generated Synthetic Content, Guoxinban Tongzi [2025] No. 2 (dated 7 March 2025, published 14 March 2025, in force 1 September 2025); with mandatory national standard GB 45438-2025 (issued 28 February 2025, in force 1 September 2025)

instruments.name: Interim Measures for the Administration of Anthropomorphic AI Interactive Services
instruments.original_title: 人工智能拟人化互动服务管理暂行办法
instruments.systems: AI services offering the public sustained emotional interaction that simulates human personality, thinking and communication; customer service, Q&A, work, education and research services are excluded only where they involve no sustained emotional interaction (Art. 2); AI is not defined
instruments.trigger: Offering such services to the public in mainland China; security assessment on launch, major change or reaching 1 million registered or 100,000 monthly active users (Art. 22); in force 15 July 2026
instruments.duties: Transparency; Labelling; Risk management; Audit; Data governance; Registration or filing; Prohibition
instruments.duty_note: Tell users they are interacting with AI and label content, remind users after two hours of continuous use, protect interaction data, audit handling of minors' data, file algorithms and bar virtual partner or relative services for minors
instruments.enf: The CAC coordinates and NDRC, MIIT, MPS, SAMR and press-and-publication departments supervise within their remits (Art. 4); cyberspace, development-and-reform, industry-and-IT and public-security departments hold interview and penalty powers (Arts. 29-30); provincial cyberspace offices receive security assessments (Art. 22)
instruments.remedy: Penalties under relevant laws and administrative regulations first (Art. 1 cites the Cybersecurity, Data Security and Personal Information Protection Laws); where none applies, cyberspace, industry-and-IT and public-security departments may warn, criticise, order rectification and suspend registrations, and for refusal or serious cases order cessation with a fine of RMB 10,000-100,000, or RMB 100,000-200,000 where life or health is endangered and harm results (Art. 30)
instruments.gap: Coverage turns on whether a service 'involves sustained emotional interaction', an undefined test that leaves general-purpose assistants used for companionship in uncertain territory; its own fines (up to RMB 200,000) apply only where no law provides, so deterrence rests on borrowed statutes.
instruments.citation: Order No. 21 of the CAC, NDRC, MIIT, MPS and SAMR, Interim Measures for the Administration of Anthropomorphic AI Interactive Services (adopted 2 February 2026, promulgated 10 April 2026, in force 15 July 2026)
